subject: Implementor-defined exception conditions, EC-IMP-xxx (specification and meaning of xxx)
notes: A.1 item 99 (optional; documented if provided; Table 13, ISO 1989:2023 14.6.13.1.1 'There are two types of level-3 of implementor-defined exception-names', cite.py --check OK). NOT PROVIDED, and the compiler now says so: ExceptionCatalog.TryGet resolves no EC-IMP-suffix name, so RAISE EXCEPTION / >>TURN / USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION on EC-IMP-WIBBLE are COBOL0711 (negatives pb1531-ec-imp-suffix-raise/-turn/-use, run on this tree; the >>TURN one reports the directive's line). The level-2 name EC-IMP stays valid (golden 2002/l1_dns_a1_99_ec_imp_level2_valid) and the SPELLING stays reserved in directives (8.12). The catalog agrees with the row: EcImplementorNamesDocumentationDriftTests.Item99_NoEcImpSuffixNameExists. GnuCOBOL 3.2's EC-IMP level-3 set is closed too (libcob/exception.def) and cobc rejects any other name in a TURN list. kb/Work PB1531 w1015w.
